chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Among what Musa (peace be upon him) whispered to his Lord was that he said: 'O Lord, what is for the one who escorts a coffin?' He said: 'I assign to him an angel from My angels, with them are banners, escorting them from their graves to their place of gathering.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for escorting a funeral procession in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a divine conversation (*munajat*) between Prophet Musa and God, highlighting the spiritual elevation of those who escort a funeral procession. God promises that angels bearing banners will accompany the individual from their grave to the place of resurrection, symbolizing honor and divine recognition. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the communal and spiritual rewards of participating in funeral rites, linking earthly acts of piety to eternal celestial honor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Among what Musa<sup>as</sup> whispered to his<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> was that he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is for the one who escorts a coffin?’ He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “I<sup>azwj</sup> Allocate and Angel from My<sup>azwj</sup> Angels to be with him, there being banners with them. They would be escorting them from their graves up to their Resurrection (Plains)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One of the private conversations that Moses had with his Lord was this: “O Lord, what is the reward for one who escorts a deceased person?” The Lord said, “I assign angels of My angels who carry banners when escorting them from their graves to the station for Judgment.’”
